How to make AI data centres more sustainable

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1301 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M.
  • Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • Industry observers note that is the climate totally cooked?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Industry observers note that is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Recent findings suggest that people have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

Future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

The Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres currently consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency says.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Industry observers note that there are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

Sources indicate that but none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that newly introduced energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

Recent findings suggest that many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of new energy needed to power data centres.

How much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

How much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

According to recent reports, one solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any upcoming generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

In a recent development, there is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a blueprint for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI declared what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the company can work around peaks in power demand.

Meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

These are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any upcoming energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

Sources indicate that there are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

Latest system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.
  • In a recent development, there were, however, some noticeable improvements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

In a recent development, there were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent plan for creating chances.

Recent findings suggest that but the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a new manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace.

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel problems in January but they at the moment sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

Sources indicate that new boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

‘That was the big positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’.

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

According to recent reports, coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat.

Industry observers note that anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

In a recent development, that is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant concern.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition quickly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni.

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

The Coventry boss stated: ‘It’s a substantial win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s important to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’.

Industry News: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1262 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
  • The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.
  • "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner declared after the talks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

"We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner declared after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia remarked a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy.".

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," states Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing.".

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia noted at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

According to recent reports, "Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she remarked. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases.".

Industry observers note that osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

She blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist notes.

Industry observers note that ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on new US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia.".

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov stated the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

"The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov remarked.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," says Artjom Bronzhukov.

Industry observers note that the expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very rapidly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

Sources indicate that "Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but states it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy mentioned he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been confirmed so far.

Iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

In a recent development, pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the issue is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that so where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

As the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

Industry observers note that carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, said he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

It has been revealed that equally, the prospect of more upheaval in the dugout might elicit little more than a shrug from fans pointing the finger squarely at the ownership and the executives they have appointed. The players were spared this time but Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers remained the target of sustained abuse as did Jason Wilcox, the director of football.

Defeat here extended United’s winless run to nine matches, their worst sequence for 38 years. They have taken just four points from the last 21 on offer in the Premier League and seem to be sinking fast. Carrick was asked about the team becoming mired in a relegation battle. This is the territory United are in.

According to recent reports, the strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

In a recent development, chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

It has been revealed that take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

Sources indicate that there were shades of the manner in which Rayan ran past him a week earlier in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win at Old Trafford. Rayan missed the chance but Rogers did no such thing, dinking the ball over Senne Lammens.

Michael Carrick said he expects to be in charge of Manchester United next week despite Lisandro Martinez’s moment of madness leaving the club mired in a relegation battle and on their worst run for 38 years.

In a recent development, having been booked moments earlier for a foul on Morgan Rogers, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow. Joe Cole, the former Chelsea and England forward, believes United must get rid of Martinez.

What do football fans actually want from their club owners? The model for most has been Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan and friends at Manchester City, owners whose hands are put frequently into pockets of unlimited depth, have made vast improvements to every aspect of the club and its community and are rarely ever seen, let alone heard from.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Chelsea, who start the day in fifth, and 16th-placed Manchester United at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday and Monday it seemed certain that Michael Carrick would be relieved of his duties before today’s game but has survived for now, hoping to turn things around in the no man’s land that sometimes resembles a vote of confidence and at others a stay of execution.

Thirty years ago when Newcastle United were coming off the bridle in the title race with Manchester United, Alex Ferguson, as he then was, accused a Leeds team, who had been in freefall since the new year, of professional malpractice when they put in a rare display of passionate commitment and tenacity at Old Trafford in a 1-0 defeat.

“Why are they not in the top six?” asked Ferguson. “To me they’re cheating their manager. You wait and see the difference when they play Newcastle.” The hate between the Leeds and Manchester united fanbases was such, he implied, that they had decided to put a shift in because, for once, they feared the consequences if they had not. It seems to this observer that the boot is now on the other foot. These Manchester United players roused themselves to fight at Elland Road then chucked it in against Como and Bournemouth. If that’s not “cheating their manager”, what is?

In a recent development, carrick will have to hope that some of the old hostility between Chelsea and Manchester United might encourage the players to run about a bit this afternoon and, at the very least, get stuck in rather than crumple spinelessly as they did last week. I doubt it would be enough to save Carrick’s job in the medium term but at least it would address whether they could stake a claim to be part of the rebuilding process.

According to recent reports, as for Chelsea, who were awful in defeat by Brentford and Spurs either side of impressive victories over Bournemouth and at Everton, they need to find some defensive solidity, discipline and a way of terrorising defences in the absence of Joao Pedro. They are a work in progress still, in the fifth year of the hedge fund hegemony. For all that attacking talent and Moises Caicedo’s ability to steamroll midfielders, their defence does not inspire confidence and last year’s petulance continues to simmer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gerry Cardinale has described Endrick as one of the best players in the world in his position, although he insists Milan’s project is bigger than any one player.

Speaking to MilanNews.it ahead of Sunday’s game against Frosinone at San Siro, the Rossoneri owner confirmed Milan will spend in January, but only on signings that fit the club’s looks.

“We’re ready. We’re doing a lot of work. As we discussed, it’s complicated, and the January transfer market is always tricky, so you have to be prepared and opportunistic,” Cardinale said. “One thing I can admit is that we’re not making any decisions we don’t feel great about. We’re going to spend money, but we’re going to spend it smartly, consistent with the project and in close coordination with Ruben and the guys here at Milanello.”.

Milan have been strongly linked with Endrick, with reports suggesting they’re ready to meet Real Madrid’s €60m valuation, but Club Brugge’s Nicolò Tresoldi is also being considered as an alternative.

Industry observers note that “Look, that name is also mentioned a lot. This project is more than just one player,” Cardinale stated. “He is one of the best players, if not the best player, in the world in his position. I have a tremendous amount of respect for him. We’ll see what’s possible in the market.”.

In a recent development, cardinale wouldn’t confirm Markus Krösche’s arrival as head of football. Corriere dello Sport has reported that the Eintracht Frankfurt director will start on 1 January.

It has been revealed that “You guys are very focused on Markus Krösche. That name has been bandied about. When we’re ready to make an announcement, I’ll come back to you on that.”.

He also spoke warmly about Adrien Rabiot, who is in talks over a upcoming contract.

Industry observers note that “I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. I think he’s fantastic, and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and his family. We’re in discussions and I hope we’ll get a good result. If it were up to me, he’d be a franchise player for this team.”.

Fourth-placed Milan face sixth-placed Frosinone on Sunday at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT].

“We’ve had a great couple of days and great sessions at Casa Milan on the January market, and on all our plans for the rest of this season and into next summer,” Cardinale added. “The mood here is really upbeat. We had a great practice today, and the team is really coming together. I spoke to a lot of the players, and they understand, as Ruben stated, how important this game is. Hopefully we come out strong and get the win.”.

#48650. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (805 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you.
  • The Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday.
  • "We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

The Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

His organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

According to recent reports, A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

It has been revealed that online games that encourage consumers to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Industry observers note that marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these latest rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

For Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

"But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch stated. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests.".

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game.".

For Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he noted.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation.".

Even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the problems consumers currently face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she noted.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding fresh rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

BEUC director Agustin Reyna disagrees.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna said.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the new legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a manufacturer's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

Sources indicate that the European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

"It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," said Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

In a recent development, agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he notes. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people.".

David Moyes was presented with a commemorative frame ahead of Monday night’s Premier League away fixture against Brentford – a record-breaking match for the Everton manager.

The trip to the Gtech Community Stadium will mark Moyes’ 593rd game as Everton manager, taking him ahead of the legendary Harry Catterick in the all-time rankings.

Everton captain James Tarkowski and former Blues midfielder Leon Osman were on hand to present the signed frame – and Moyes noted it’s a “privilege and honour” to have reached the historic milestone.

"I'm really thrilled about. I've become the manager who has managed more Everton games than anyone before. That's a privilege and an honour to be put in that position.

Industry observers note that "I have to thank the people who brought me to the Club in the first place. When you take a chance on a young manager, you never know it'll be work, but they had great faith and believed in me.

"I'm so thankful for the people around Everton because they've been so good for me.".

Handing over the frame, Osman said: “It’s a record I don’t think will ever be beaten – and I don’t say that lightly. This is some achievement for a huge football club.

“I’m sure James is like me in saying it’s been an honour to play for you. It’s been an honour, a privilege. It’s been hard! But you’ve made us all better and we wish you many more successes for the upcoming seasons.”.

Cesc Fabregas praised Jacobo Ramón’s attacking threat after the defender scored in Como’s 2-0 win over Cagliari, although he insisted the performance was far from perfect.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, Ramón headed Como in front from Yan Couto’s assist in the 24th minute, and Lucas Da Cunha added a second, also set up by Couto, early in the second half. The win takes Fabregas’ side up to fourth for now, and Como remain unbeaten at the Sinigaglia in Serie A this season.

“Perfect? No. We conceded four counter-attacks, three of them significant chances where they could have scored,” Fabregas stated. “They did something different going forward and found space in behind us, but from around the 35th minute things changed, and in the second half there was only one team on the pitch.

Industry observers note that “I’m very happy for the lads. There was so much energy, and Lahdo came on very well. We had to finish with two right-backs because we don’t have the players. Today my only attacking option on the bench was Nico Paz.”.

Ramón has just been called up by Spain for the first time, and Fabregas believes his scoring has improved a lot.

Recent findings suggest that “There are players who are stronger, but he’s a player I like. I won’t say too much about how I feel about him, because he might read it later,” Fabregas joked. “We worked a lot on his finishing. Last year he couldn’t score in front of goal, even easy chances. Now he scores them. It shows you they’re kids, but they improve every year.

Industry observers note that “He arrives in the box with more aggression than a striker, even when you don’t expect it, and he can play long and short. In the air, he’s first or second in Serie A for duels won. But if you want to reach the top, you have to handle Thuram and Esposito, so the lads understand they always have to do more to get to that level.

Sources indicate that “In five or six years, I’d like to see all these lads playing at World Cups and winning the Champions League. They have the chance to grow here.”.

Da Cunha started despite his efforts with France this week, because Maxence Caqueret picked up a minor problem on Friday.

“Honestly, I wanted to rest him today, but we can’t take risks now, we’re down to 11, 12, 13 players. He’s a gem for us. He always raises the level. I’d like every player in the world to have Da Cunha’s mentality.”.

He also warned there’s no room to ease off.

“There are seven games left before Christmas, and everyone has to play their part.”.

Wouter Vrancken stated Hearts’ ruthless 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

Sources indicate that the 47-year-old mentioned: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park.

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

'Today they did it and hopefully they felt it can work and they can show it more.

Recent findings suggest that 'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'.

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

According to recent reports, he noted: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and shows grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

'I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.'.

Now, 30 years later, Mitre has reimagined the legendary ball, bringing it back with a modern twist.

The newly introduced Ultimax Pro 30th Anniversary Ball merges the classic design with cutting-edge technology, celebrating its iconic status while setting a new standard for the next generation.

In a recent development, while the ball retains the familiar 6-panel construction, the classic white, blue, and red colourway, and the unmistakable crown logo, itâs been upgraded with advanced features. Hyperflow grooves reduce drag and a sleek pearl finish offers a nod to traditional 30th-anniversary gifts. The interior also sees improvements, with Hyperfoam cushioning now enhanced for cleaner strikes and even more power.

To mark the milestone, Mitre has launched the "The Next In Line" campaign, spotlighting the latest wave of football talent carrying on their family legacies.

The campaign features rising stars such as Raphaella Wright-Phillips, granddaughter of Arsenal icon Ian Wright, Ruben Butt, son of Manchester United legend Nicky Butt, and Jacob Fowler, whose father is Liverpoolâs own Robbie Fowler.

The trio, each in vintage 95/96 kits, embody the connection between the past and the future â just as the fresh Ultimax Pro does itself.

EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.
  • When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.
  • The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.

When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi, followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy.

Zelenskyy and Kushner also stated Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.

It has been revealed that kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine, alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.

"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.

But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.

Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.

In a recent development, "Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations.".

Europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.

"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.

European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.

Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa said in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.

Putin noted a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove new joiners Finland and Sweden, could be among his demands.

In a recent development, "What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately.".

This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of, especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.

Sources indicate that "Right now, we are in the [Russian] trap," said Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal. "If something is a threat to you, will you discuss your defense with the threat [itself]?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump remarked publicly that he was hoping for a "very big, beautiful agreement" that "might involve all of Europe.".

Zelensky noted he found the US approach "a bit strange.".

Many of Europe's leaders speaking in Dublin referenced previous agreements with Russia that they believe Moscow has breached.

They include the 1975 Helsinki Accords, the 1990 Paris Charter, 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act and the one they consider most crucial: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which forbids Russia from using force against Ukraine unless in self-defense.

The rancor over the seat at the peace talks is drawing focus away from arguably the bigger battle in the EU now ― how to fund Ukraine as the war continues.

Back in October, the European Commission identified a €70 billion hole in the EU’s funding it had promised for Ukraine’s economy.

Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico has opposed any further financial and military support for Ukraine.

But Germany's Merz warned he could block the EU's next seven-year budget unless member states agree to contribute to Ukraine's financing.

Arsenal reportedly prefer RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa over Brentford winger Kevin Schade as they look at both players as targets for January.

The Gunners are still keen to strengthen out wide in the near future after missing out on top targets such as Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers during the summer.

The main names being linked with Arsenal now are Nusa and Schade, but football.london journalist Tom Canton says the clear preference out of those two is the Leipzig wide-man.

Nusa has established himself as one of the most exciting young talents in Europe in recent times, with the Norway international already on six goals and seven assists so far this season.

Industry observers note that “Yes, there is interest in Kevin Schade,” Canton remarked in a football.london Q&A. “He is not their first choice for a left-winger, with Antonio Nusa higher up the list, but the German is certainly appreciated.”.

It will be interesting to see how this saga develops, but one imagines there’ll be a lot of takers for both of these in-form attacking players in the coming weeks and months.

Nusa perhaps looks like he has the higher ceiling as he’s still only 21 years of age, but Schade has the advantage of being proven in the Premier League already.

It could be an interesting January for Arsenal, with the Premier League champions also linked with strikers such as Julian Alvarez and Nicolo Tresoldi.

The north London giants could also lose one or two players, as there’s some uncertainty over Martin Zubimendi as he’s linked with the likes of Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, and Chelsea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paris Saint-Germain fear Désiré Doue has suffered a serious knee injury, a fresh blow for Luis Enrique days before Roma visit the Parc des Princes in the Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that according to Foot Mercato, the 21-year-old’s right knee gave way while he was shielding the ball, with no contact from an opponent, late in the first half of Saturday’s Ligue 1 game at Nice. He had scored to make it 2-1 only minutes earlier.

In a recent development, doué left the pitch in tears on a stretcher and was replaced by Ferran Torres. PSG are waiting for scans to confirm how serious the injury is, but Foot01 report that the club fear a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament.

Industry observers note that if confirmed, it would be a second major knee injury in barely a month for the European champions. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the ACL in his right knee in October’s 4-2 win over Barcelona and is expected to miss most of the season. Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos also suffered thigh injuries in that game.

Doué had only just returned from an earlier injury when he joined up with France this month.

PSG are chasing a third consecutive Champions League title, and they host Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma on Wednesday at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT]. Whatever the scans show, Doué is very unlikely to face the Giallorossi.
